qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Prestige fragrance and makeup house (Carolina Herrera, Rabanne, Jean Paul Gaultier, Charlotte Tilbury, Byredo). While gross margins are ~74%, the business model relies heavily on fashion-driven fragrance trends, third-party fashion house licenses vulnerable to non-renewal or poaching by larger conglomerates (e.g. historical loss of Prada and Valentino to L'Oréal), and trend-sensitive celebrity makeup (Charlotte Tilbury). Lacks a multi-cycle public track record of pricing power through deep recessions.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3 (3b = N, REJECT). Prestige fragrance and makeup portfolio heavily exposed to fashion novelty cycles, influencer makeup volatility (Charlotte Tilbury), and licensing fragility where major luxury houses can defect or bring beauty in-house (as demonstrated by past losses of Prada and Valentino to L'Oréal). Lacks proven multi-cycle pricing power as a standalone public company.
qualitative.evidence: May 2024 IPO with dual-class family voting control. Revenues grew to €4.79B in 2024 with 20.2% EBITDA margins, but ROIC compressed from 22% in 2023 to ~16% in 2024 following M&A step-ups (Dr. Barbara Sturm, Charlotte Tilbury stake increase to 78.5%). Substantial non-renewal and renegotiation risks on licensed brands vs owner-monopolists like Hermès or L'Oréal.
